correctness.rationale: For n between successive factorials, uniform first-round occupancy has maximal load m-1,m,or m+1 with high probability. Factorial-moment variance controls ensure that the number of second-place boxes exceeds the number of highest boxes by a factor at least c m/log m. The selected O(m^4) cells have multinomial total weight O(m^6/n) and hence independent Poisson TV error O(m^12/n). The Poisson means differ by O(m) while individual standard deviations are order m; a moderate-deviation threshold produces vanishing first-leader exceedance probability but diverging expected number of runner-up exceedances. Uniform tail bounds and independence give strict turnover along all integers, including ties. A published second-round winner-containment result supplies only the distinct corollary. The direct proof, error uniformity, boundary cases and exact finite verifier were reviewed; finite checks are not misused as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The published primary source explicitly presents loss of initial leader predictability at the first critical reinforcement exponent as conjectural. Strict turnover resolves that boundary question as a corollary and provides a stronger mechanism theorem with all ties and all integer sizes. The crowd-of-runners-up extreme-value mechanism is structurally informative and not an arbitrary small-parameter computation. Practical finite n rates are not asserted.
